title: Silver agent-led adoption plan v1
description: What an existing repository contains, what an agent thinks each entry is, and what the designer decided to do about it — one entry at a time. Silver enumerates and validates; the agent reads and proposes; the human decides. Nothing here can move, rename, delete, or rewrite a file that already exists: adoption is additive, and the disposition vocabulary is deliberately small enough to keep it that way.

target.description: The workspace being adopted into. Absolute, because a plan is produced and applied from different working directories.

source.description: A second repository being read for translation, such as a product codebase whose UI, components, or documentation inform design artifacts here. Read-only without exception: no disposition writes anything inside a source.

discovered.description: What Silver found, and nothing about what it means. Paths, kinds, and sizes only — every judgement about an entry belongs to the agent in `items`.

truncated.description: This directory holds more entries than the walk reported. Stated rather than silently trimmed, so nothing looks smaller than it is.

skipped_directories.description: Directory names excluded from the walk — dependencies, build output, caches. Listed so their absence is a stated choice rather than a gap.

items.description: One decision per file or directory. An item without an `accepted` decision is never applied.

observed.description: What the agent actually saw. Facts about the entry, separate from what it concludes.

agent_reading.description: What the agent thinks this is. Kept separate from `observed` so a wrong conclusion is visibly a conclusion.

proposed_disposition.description: leave-in-place: no change. register-in-place: name it in the manifest where it sits. link-as-source: pin it as a linked or guidance source. as-references: bring it in as reference material rather than truth. translate: write a new Silver artifact derived from it, original untouched. ignore: seen and deliberately not adopted, so re-runs stop asking.

artifact.description: How a `register-in-place` entry enters the manifest. It points at the existing path; the file is not read, moved, or rewritten.

link.description: How a `link-as-source` entry is registered. The agent supplies the judgement — what it is and who owns it — and Silver computes the revision and integrity pins, because those are facts to be measured rather than claims to be accepted.

target_path.description: Where a `translate` or `as-references` output is written. Must not already exist — Silver writes it exclusively, so a collision aborts rather than overwrites.

content.description: The new artifact's full content, authored by the agent. Silver is the only writer, which is what makes the no-overwrite rule enforceable rather than merely promised.

decision.description: Filled by the human, one item at a time. Only `accepted` is applied; `rejected` becomes leave-in-place; `deferred` is asked again next run.

questions.description: One ready-made question per undecided entry, in the shape every host already renders for setup. Emitted by `adopt inspect` so a per-entry conversation needs no new presentation code, and carried through apply so a plan stays self-describing.
